question: Does the frozen adaptive Rminus response on the two N505 child geometries contain a spatial component not exhausted by its defined-rate profile, and does it escape an ordinary positive Fourier spatial cone adversary?

geometry.common_field: one Bernoulli field on parent_site x fiber, transported to both children
geometry.sampling: one uniform nonzero residue per replica; residue 0 excluded before reveal to avoid marked-location collision

adaptive_rule.support: unique nearest transferable vertex from the state-dependent D or J source component toward the landing point

source_frozen_definition_model.model: E[Rminus(j)]=alpha*Pr(defined(j)) jointly over plus/minus and j<->-j

frozen_tests.primary: joint covariance-whitened zero test of Rminus-alpha*defined at p<0.01
frozen_tests.adversary: joint covariance-whitened nonnegative cosine cone with separate plus/minus spectra and 500 Gaussian bootstrap replicates
frozen_tests.periodogram: full batch-covariant cosine coefficients for Rminus and defined profiles
frozen_tests.stop: stop after 20k unless the primary definition-only model is rejected; do not enlarge based on the cone alone

claim_boundary: The positive Fourier cone is an ordinary spatial-state adversary, not an exact constraint on adaptive intervention response. Rejection does not identify a field, state count, or path memory.
